extracted.intended_audience: short-story authors, editors, and literary critics (readers of an annual yearbook)
extracted.subtask_description: Critical criteria and selection rules used in an annual literary yearbook to judge and rank American short stories (qualities of craft, style, realization, and periodical-level metrics). Includes the asterisk system marking distinction and magazine ranking metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fusion of plot and characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: The fusion of plot and characterization in a fully realized picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A story should integrate plot and characterization so that the picture is fully realized; the author employs sharply contrasted dramatic values to achieve this fusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological realism and reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Portrayal of psychological reactions upon characters (e.g., the reactions of nearest kin to an execution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memorable stories depict believable psychological reactions and inner life; intense, mordant studies that etch psychological detail can have strong power and vigor of expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / new voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Work by a new and original artist that inaugurates a new craftsmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original, abnormal, or unlikely stories may not be popular but can be important if they realize a fullness of vision and introduce novel techniques or perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realization / completeness of substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete realization of a story's substance — fully rendering its subject-matter and emotional values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with slight substance, an author can dignify material by deftly hinting at values and leaving the rest to the reader; complete realization endows the author with adequate means of telling the tale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of narrative force / form
rubrics_metrics.description: Economy in narrative — avoiding prolixity and unnecessary material; telling with essential material only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should show economy (of narrative force or form), reducing action to essentials so passion may be revealed in an 'eternal instant'; one critic notes lack of economy as a shortcoming even when the piece has vivid pictorial qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power and sincerity of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: A story's power and sincerity can compel admiration even if the critic personally dislikes its taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power and sincerity in presentation — e.g., moving the reader to 'unwilling admiration' — are important virtues even when subject/taste is contestable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect suggestion vs direct statement (show, don't tell)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rendering character by indirect suggestion rather than by direct statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fondness for observation of minute, revelatory details and indirect suggestion can reveal character more effectively than explicit statement; this technique often reduces action in favor of suggestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection / gift of selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The author's ability to select appropriate material and details (freshness of vision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fine artist shows admirable selection, bringing freshness of vision to familiar substance; selection helps dignify slight material and make it interesting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of contrast to reveal character
rubrics_metrics.description: Power of contrast permitted to reveal finer grain in character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast (dramatic, psychological, social) is an instrument to show subtlety and finer traits of character; it can be central to distinguished realist studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid pictorial quality / realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong, vivid pictorial narrative that renders reality (even brutal/ruthless depictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vivid, pictorial narration can be appalling in its brutality but still artistically justified if it fuses passion and substance into form; such realism may lack economy but still reach high imaginative/spiritual power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passion fused into artistic form
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorial passion that fuses substance into notable artistic form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when techniques are harsh or rudely pictorial, the author's passion can elevate material into a distinctive artistic achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenderness and quiet emotional integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Tenderness that interprets human life with quiet emotional integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A tender, restrained approach can yield strong human values; quiet emotional integrity distinguishes realistic portrayals done without sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding sentimentalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Resisting excessive sentimentality while still achieving emotional values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A story should gain emotional force without lapsing into sentimentality; handled skillfully this yields truthfulness and lasting portraits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leisurely vs concentrated narrative tempo
rubrics_metrics.description: Tempo — whether leisurely/old-fashioned or concentrated — must suit substance; leisurely narration can still be competently realized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A slower unfolding may be appropriate for certain subjects (reticence, undercurrent of humor), provided the substance is fresh and characterization interesting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short story as poetic virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetic virtues (passion, magic, truth, economy, background) applied to short fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A story may possess virtues of poetry (rich characterization, background, dramatic power) and still function as a short story; economy of form with richness of background is prized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested mystery and subtle psychological etching
rubrics_metrics.description: Skillful suggestion of mystery, bitingly etched psychology, and dramatic contrast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that suggest more than they state and use psychological sketching effectively are ranked among the finer short stories of the year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horror realized with persuasive presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A completely realized study of horror with persuasive presentation and compelling movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Horror that is unforgettable must make its substance feel awfully real and present it persuasively; an ending may be inconclusive as life is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological study of a fixed idea with sufficient background
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtle psychological studies of fixed ideas rendered with faithfulness to premises and sufficiency of background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persuasiveness depends on the reader granting certain premises and on a poignant sufficiency of background to sustain the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmosphere/dreamlike veil for supernatural effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a veil (distance) between action and reader to weave an illusive, romantic substance that remains real to the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dreamlike atmosphere should be balanced: outline not too faint and details not overemphasized; deliberate restraint achieves intended effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mannerism vs developing style
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that mannerism can mark a transition from affectation to true style; mannered pieces may still be valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mannered piece can be seen as transitional if style begins to match substance; prolixity can be tolerated if it carries passionate reality and faithfulness to subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sympathy for less-expressed emotions / background preoccupation
rubrics_metrics.description: A preoccupation with backgrounds and sympathy for less-expressed emotions yields subtly toned studies of adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing traditions (e.g., Henry James') of nuanced background and emotional nuance are assessed positively when carried competently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity of approach and sympathetic reticence
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplicity of approach and sympathetic reticence can confer rich human values on tawdry substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even tawdry subjects can gain dignity and richness if handled with simple, restrained narrative power and not loosely put together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrained art and suggestiveness in ghost stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Treating familiar ghost-story substance with restrained art and suggestiveness of unspoken things fused with environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restraint and harmony between landscape/environment and narrative strangeness can elevate a familiar genre piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grim passion and unsophisticated art
rubrics_metrics.description: A grim passion allied with unsophisticated art can effectively tell a tale of fate or war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when echoes of other works exist, complete realization of substance can make the story stand on its own and indicate future promise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asterisks system for indicating distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: One, two, and three asterisks are employed to indicate relative distinction; three-asterisk stories are of somewhat permanent literary value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three asterisks indicate permanent literary value and, for American authors, entitlement to placement on the annual 'Roll of Honor.' The lists exclude reprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluding reprints in assessment lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Reprints are excluded from the lists of distinctive and starred stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only original first-publication stories are counted when assigning asterisks and when compiling periodical averages and rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazine-level metrics: counts and percentages of distinctive stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative measurement by number of distinctive stories published and percentage of distinctive stories among total stories published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodicals are ranked both by the sheer number of distinctive stories and by the percentage (distinctive/total) — these two metrics produce different rankings and are reported separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking rules and tie-breaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Ties in ranking lists are decided by taking relative rank in other lists into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When two periodicals tie on a metric, their ranks in the other compiled lists (e.g., percentage vs number) are used to break ties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thresholds for publishing ranking tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Only periodicals that published over a threshold (e.g., more than twenty-five stories and exceeding an average of 75% in stories of distinction) are included in certain ranked tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The yearbook limits some tables to periodicals meeting minimum publication count and quality percentage thresholds to ensure meaningful comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and metadata conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexing conventions: prefixed asterisks indicate distinction; an asterisk before an author name indicates he is not an American; specific abbreviations are used for periodicals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent bibliographic abbreviations and marking of nationality are part of the selection/indexing protocol to maintain clarity in lists and the Roll of Honor.
